newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FOCUS-Avgold may downsize after poor Q1.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Avgold may downsize after poor Q1.

text.p: Avgold Ltd could downsize certain operations due to unacceptably low operating margins, the South African gold mining group said on Tuesday.

Announcing disappointing first quarter gold results, Avgold said that production for the current June quarter was unlikely to improve and that it was looking closely at its Loraine Gold Mines and Hartebeestfontein Gold Mining Co.
"There is no way I will allow the operations in Avgold to detract from the future of Avgold," managing director Jurie Geldenhuys said at a presentation.
The group's total gold profit before capital expenditure fell to 382 million rand from 460 million rand.
Loraine slid into a 4.96 million rand loss from 5.42 million rand profit and Hartebeestfontein shrank its gold profit to 20.02 million rand from 101.35 million rand previously.
"It has been a most disappointing quarter and a sobering experience," Geldenhuys said.
"Loraine will not be allowed to be a drain and I'm sure we'll have to make a decision on that this quarter," he said.
Director of operations Tim Spindler said the poor first quarter performance was largely due to public holidays which cut shifts worked to 65 from 74 in the previous quarter.
He added that matters were made worse by a six week-long underground fire at Hartebeestfontein's No 6 shaft, which lost it about 300 kg of gold output, and a sickly gold price.
"We are operating on margins that are unacceptable. At the current gold price our margins have almost disappeared altogether," Spindler said.

Hartebeestfontein's future was being examined and unless the mine could work more shifts -- in which case the upside potential was enormous -- a downsizing programme would have to be implemented over 18 months, he said.

This would entail the already planned closure of the No 4 shaft as well as the unplanned closure of the No 5 shaft, bringing the milling rate of the mine down to about 240,000 tonnes per month from its current 400,000 tonnes per month.

"We have a vision of a smaller operation milling about 160,000 tonnes per month. Harties is an old mine and the travelling time (from surface to rock face) is excessive. Production at Harties is declining and not just in number of shifts worked," Spindler said.
Avgold would be meeting with its miners' unions on May 8 and hoped to get a commitment from them on improving production.
"We have to get everybody to agree on ways of operating our mines on a full calendar basis," Spindler said.
Loraine's future as a stand-alone operation was in the balance with it becoming more and more a marginal mine.

"The marginal nature of Loraine has been highlighted. This quarter (June) does not promise to be any better than the last. The options for Loraine as a stand-alone operation are becoming increasingly limited," Spindler said.
"This crisis could force us into short-term drastic action. Loraine does not have a very bright future but its potential role in Target has significant growth opportunities," he said.

The Target gold project is not yet a producing mine but its exploration development and shaft sinking is on schedule and projects manager Roger Dixon said tonnage and grade data so far were encouraging.
Capital expenditure in the current quarter for the three mines was likely to be in the region of 14 to 16 million rand.
